Class ConceptMapLoader

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.support.map.ConceptMapLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
MappingLoader
Direct Known Subclasses:
ConceptMapJsonLoader, ConceptMapXmlLoader
public abstract class ConceptMapLoader extends Object implements MappingLoader
Shared implementation for the two MappingLoaders that read FHIR R4 ConceptMap resources: ConceptMapJsonLoader for *.conceptmap.r4.json and ConceptMapXmlLoader for *.conceptmap.r4.xml. Everything below the parser is the same for both, since the wire format is a matter of encoding, not of content.

There is one loader per wire format rather than one that reads both, because a format id selects exactly one loader and so has to say which encoding to expect. A ConceptMap fetched from a terminology server carries no file name to decide it. The FHIR version is part of both the ids and the extensions so that a loader for another version can sit on the same classpath.

Most of IPF's mappings are concept maps, and for consumers who already govern their terminology in ConceptMap - authored in Simplifier or Forge, shipped in an Implementation Guide, validated by the FHIR validator. This loader lets IPF read that artifact directly instead of duplicating it as an internal table. It is offered as a loader, not as IPF's own format: the same mapping is a third longer in ConceptMap JSON than in the XML format, comments have nowhere natural to go, and two of the model's five fallback modes need an extension, so an IPF-flavored ConceptMap is not fully portable anyway.

Parsing is HAPI's job. This loader only walks group -> element -> target into Mapping records and reads the IPF extensions.

Field alignment

How the model maps onto ConceptMap
ModelConceptMap
keySystemgroup.source
valueSystemgroup.target
entry.key -> entry.valuegroup.element.code -> ...target.code
entry.equivalence...target.equivalence
unmatched identity / fixedgroup.unmapped.mode provided / fixed
unmatched functionextension ConceptMapExtensions.UNMAPPED_FUNCTION
reverseUnmatchedextension ConceptMapExtensions.REVERSE_UNMAPPED
reversibleextension ConceptMapExtensions.REVERSIBLE
nameextension ConceptMapExtensions.MAPPING_NAME, else derived from the canonical, see below

Mapping names

A group carrying the ConceptMapExtensions.MAPPING_NAME extension is named by it. Otherwise the name is derived from the ConceptMap's canonical identity rather than from its name, which is a label publishers change between releases:
  • the base is the last segment of url, falling back to name and then id for a ConceptMap without one;
  • a version is appended as |version, as in a FHIR canonical reference, so that several versions of one ConceptMap can be loaded side by side - kdl-ihe-classcode|2024 next to kdl-ihe-classcode|2025;
  • a ConceptMap with a single group becomes one mapping named by the base;
  • in a ConceptMap with several groups, every group is named by the base plus # and the last segment of its target - kdl-ihe-classcode|2025#IHEXDSclassCode and kdl-ihe-classcode|2025#v3-NullFlavor. No group is privileged: FHIR gives their order no meaning, and naming by target keeps the names stable when a release inserts or reorders groups. The base then names a composite of all groups in declaration order, which answers like FHIR's $translate without a target system: with the first group declaring the code, and only if none does, with the first group whose unmapped answers. Mappings.translate(String, String) says which group's target system the answer belongs to.
A ConceptMap whose groups all carry the ConceptMapExtensions.MAPPING_NAME extension - which is how ConceptMapWriter writes mappings - holds exactly the mappings its groups name, and no composite is added: its author said what the mappings are called.

So a caller consuming a third-party ConceptMap needs to know neither which groups it has nor which one holds a code: it asks the base. A caller wanting one target system specifically asks that group. An other-map fallback refers to a ConceptMap by canonical and resolves to the base the same way, so http://x/ConceptMap/base|2025 delegates to base|2025, and http://x/ConceptMap/base to the only version of base registered.

R4 only. If R5 support lands it follows IPF's existing pattern - a parallel module whose loaders claim *.conceptmap.r5.json and the format id conceptmap-r5-json - and the only semantic difference to absorb is the rename of target.equivalence to target.relationship, which collapses onto the same Equivalence.

    • format

      public String format()
      Description copied from interface: MappingLoader
      Short, stable identifier of the format this loader reads, e.g. xml, yaml or conceptmap-r4-json. It is what a caller names to select this loader regardless of the source's file extension, and it is compared case-insensitively.

      Two loaders on one classpath must not share a format id, since the id is what picks one of them; qualify it the way conceptmap-r4-json does when a format has versions or encodings that a second loader might read.

      Specified by:
      format in interface MappingLoader
      Returns:
      the format id, never null or blank

    • supports

      public boolean supports(URI source)
      Description copied from interface: MappingLoader
      Whether this loader claims a source that nobody named a format for. Implementations decide by file extension: a source it cannot recognize from its name alone is not its own, even if it could read the content, because that is what keeps dispatch predictable.
      Specified by:
      supports in interface MappingLoader
      Parameters:
      source - location of the mapping source, used for its file extension
      Returns:

    • load

      public List<Mapping> load(InputStream in, URI source, MappingFunctionRegistry functions, Consumer<String> warnings) throws IOException
      Description copied from interface: MappingLoader
      Reads all mappings contained in one source document, reporting what the model cannot hold.

      A format that can state more than the model - the legacy Groovy DSL binds arbitrary objects where the model holds strings - reports each such loss to warnings, one message per mapping, starting with the mapping's name. MappingConverter collects them. The default implementation has nothing to report.

      Specified by:
      load in interface MappingLoader
      Parameters:
      in - the source content; the caller closes the stream
      source - location of the source, for diagnostics
      functions - registry a loader may add functions to
      warnings - receives a human-readable message for every loss the loader has to make
      Returns:
      the mappings read, in declaration order
      Throws:
      IOException - if the source cannot be read
